title: Catalogue growth over time
finding: Most titles were added in 2019 (2,013). The latest year in the data, 2021, has 1,498 (74% of the peak; it may be a partial year).
action: Check first whether the drop is real or only an incomplete year. If it is real, focus the budget on fewer, higher-quality titles instead of adding volume.

title: Movies and TV shows: how the mix moves
finding: Movies are 70% of the catalogue. The TV show share of new additions went from 32% in 2015 to 34% in 2021.
action: TV shows are taking a bigger share of new titles. Series usually keep subscribers coming back every week, so keep investing in them, especially returning series.

title: Share of international content
finding: 63% of titles are not led by the USA. This share moved from 38% in 2015 to 63% in 2021. India is the biggest non-US country with 1,056 titles.
action: Keep investing in local stories from the top non-US countries, starting with India. Local titles can also be promoted to viewers in other countries.

title: Audience mix of the catalogue
finding: Adults is the biggest group with 46% of titles. Kids is the smallest with 10%.
action: Look at the Kids group first. It has the fewest titles, so adding more could reach viewers the catalogue serves less today. Check viewing data before investing.

title: How concentrated the genres are
finding: The top 3 genres (International Movies, Dramas, Comedies) make up 36% of all genre tags. The biggest is 'International Movies' with 2,751 titles.
action: Keep the strong genres, and test smaller genres that match what viewers in growing countries ask for, so the catalogue does not depend on only a few genres.

title: Age of titles when they are added
finding: A title was on average 1.3 years old when added in 2015 and 5.8 years old in 2021.
action: Netflix adds older titles more often now. Licensed older content is cheap filler, so balance it with new originals to keep the catalogue feeling fresh.

title: Additions follow a monthly pattern
finding: July is the busiest month (827 titles) and February is the quietest (562).
action: Plan big releases for February and other quiet months, so viewers have something new all year and big titles do not compete with each other.

title: Movie length and show format
finding: The middle movie runs 98 minutes and 19% of movies are longer than 2 hours. 67% of TV shows have only one season.
action: Many shows stop after one season. Look at why, since renewing the successful ones is cheaper than starting new shows.

title: Missing information in the raw data
finding: 0% of titles have no director and 0% have no country in the original file.
action: Make director and country required when titles are added. Better data gives better search, recommendations and reports.
